findings.statement: Design D-1 p. 2 and D-2 tell the maintainer to apply the patch with `git apply <path>`. Then the agent checks `git diff --cached --name-only` for exactly seven paths (also the verification of tasks 1.1). Plain `git apply` changes only the working tree: the index stays empty, so `git diff --cached` lists nothing. The new file `.github/workflows/test.yml` stays untracked, so even `git diff --name-only` lists six paths, not seven. The check as written cannot pass.
findings.recommendation: Make the maintainer's command `git apply --index <path>` (it stages the new file too), or name the step between apply and check that stages the seven paths and say who does it. Keep the verification of tasks 1.1 consistent with that step.

findings.statement: The new language sentence of rule `env` (Appendix) is absolute: 'everything in the repository and on GitHub — artifacts, code, comments, commits, PRs, issues — is English'. The Change itself states exceptions. The proposal (Impact, Non-goals) keeps the Russian specs `architecture` and `kernel`, archived Changes and `design/`. D-4 keeps the marker «❗ Выполнить» Russian, and it sits in the text of `env` and `maintainer-acts`, which `warrant sync` renders into `AGENTS.md`. The generated `.claude/agents/warrant-reviewer.md` is tracked in git (per `.gitignore`), and its body is Russian. It comes from the pinned WARRANT pack, which this Change does not touch (Non-goals). As written, the rule cannot be met. An agent that edits an existing Russian file has two readings: translate the file, or keep its language.
findings.recommendation: Scope the rule to what the project writes from now on: new artifacts, code, comments, commits, PRs and issues. Name the exceptions in the rule text: existing Russian specs until their replacing Change, archived Changes, `design/`, files generated by `warrant sync` from the WARRANT pack, and the marker «❗ Выполнить». Say what happens to an existing Russian file when it is edited (for example, the new or changed text is English, and the file is not translated as a side effect).

findings.statement: The language rule says Russian is used only in the chat with the maintainer. `design-next` SL-K03 requires the first bench set to carry 'Russian variants' of the questions. SL-S2 measures 'RU↔EN consistency' (BN-M04). Bench items are project data in the repository. Under the new rule an agent writing the S1 bench set either breaks the rule or drops the Russian variants that the design requires.
findings.recommendation: Add an exception to the `env` language sentence: corpus and bench data whose language is part of what is measured (SL-K03, BN-M04), such as Russian question variants, are allowed. Or limit the rule to prose artifacts (specs, design, code, comments, commits, PRs, issues).

findings.statement: The `process` rule addition (Appendix) says 'one AREA … = at most one active Change' but does not define 'active'. The decision it cites, SL-T08 on branch `docs/sw-milestone`, defines it: 'a second Change in the same AREA waits for the archive of the first'. It also caps the work at 'at most three Changes are in implementation at once' (grilling Q22), and says shared files are owned by the walking skeleton (Q23). The rule text drops all three. Ids are allocated as 'maximum + 1' only from what is archived or visible. A reader who takes 'active' to end at impl-PR merge (`MERGED`) will start a second Change in the AREA before archive, and that gives the `ID_DUPLICATE` and the archive overwrite the proposal sets out to prevent.
findings.recommendation: Write the boundary into the rule text: a Change is active from `warrant init change` until its archive-PR merges, and a second Change in the AREA starts only after that. Add the cap of three Changes in implementation and the skeleton ownership of shared files, or state in D-4 why they stay out of the rule.

findings.statement: The proposal says the rules are translated with 'meaning unchanged except four additions from the grilling'. D-4 cites 'Q25, Q26, Q28' for the `tracking` addition about slice state: computed and never stored, a milestone plus umbrella issue, one Claude Code session per Change started from its issue, and a coordinator session that never writes a Change's code. The launch-readiness grilling record (`design-next/reviews/2026-10-01-launch-readiness-grilled.md` on `docs/sw-milestone`) ends at Q24. Those decisions have no recorded source. The `tracking` addition also has more parts than the one item the proposal counts.
findings.recommendation: Cite where Q25/Q26/Q28 are recorded (add them to the grilling record or link the maintainer's decision). Otherwise take the coordinator and session paragraph out of this Change. List every addition to `tracking` in the proposal.

findings.statement: The proposal, design and new rule texts reference `design-next` SL-T08 and SL-T01 (the freeze-tag edits), and the record `design-next/reviews/2026-10-01-launch-readiness-grilled.md`. On `main` (5b56d83) SL-T08 does not exist and the record is absent: both exist only on the unmerged branch `docs/sw-milestone`, and grilling Q24 runs that docs PR in parallel. The Change silently assumes the docs PR merges first. If it does not, `AGENTS.md` on `main` sends every agent to a design ID that does not exist.
findings.recommendation: State the dependency: the impl-PR (or the maintainer's patch of D-2) waits for the merge of `docs/sw-milestone`. Or make the rule texts self-contained, so they do not depend on SL-T08 existing.

findings.statement: The motivation is that `main` 'was already red unnoticed once', and the job `test` on push to `main` is meant to catch that. The check is not required (protection is #20), and no actor or reaction is named for a red `test` on `main`. Nothing says who notices, what is opened (an issue, which priority) or what blocks until it is fixed. Detection without a named reaction leaves the stated problem 'red unnoticed' open.
findings.recommendation: Add one sentence to rule `tracking` or `process`: a red `test / test` on `main` → the agent that sees it opens an `infra:` issue `bug` `P1`, and no new impl-PR merges until it is green. Or name another owner and reaction.

findings.statement: The proposal (What Changes) and design (Goals, D-5) say `areas.json` is rewritten 'to the capabilities of the module matrix ST-M01' / 'one AREA per spec of the module matrix ST-M01'. The D-5 table does not follow ST-M01. ST-M01 modules are kernel, trust, measure, ledger, codec, runtime, capabilities, adapters, assembly, cli. The table adds architecture, projections, store, acts, catalog, lens and bench, which are not modules (projections, store and acts are parts of `ledger`), and it has no AREA for `assembly`. The table matches grilling Q20; the ST-M01 wording does not.
findings.recommendation: Replace 'module matrix ST-M01' with the actual source (grilling Q20 / SL-T08: one AREA per OpenSpec capability spec). Say where requirements of module `assembly` live (for example, AREA CL or AR).

findings.statement: D-5 gives AREA code `ST` to capability `store`. In `design-next`, prefix `ST-` is file 10 'Code structure' (ST-M01, ST-S01, ST-K01), which the `architecture` spec (AR) will implement. Most other codes mirror their design prefix (LG, TR, CT, LN, BN). So 'REQ-ST-…' (store) sits next to 'Implements: ST-S01' (structure) under REQ-AR-…, and SL-T03 makes those `Implements:` lines the cross-reference between them. Reading `ST` as structure is the natural mistake.
findings.recommendation: Choose a code for `store` that is not a `design-next` ID prefix (for example `SO` or `SR`), or record in D-5 why the clash is accepted.

findings.statement: The `tracking` addition says a Change's issue 'sits in the milestone of its slice', and each Change is a session 'started from the Change's issue'. Nothing covers Changes outside any slice: `infra` Changes like this one, or the small shared-file Changes of the `process` rule. Area `sw` is introduced as '(switch)' with no pointer to what the switch is (SL-T07 / SL-SW).
findings.recommendation: Say whether a Change outside a slice needs an issue and a milestone (for example, `infra` issues have no milestone). Point `sw` to SL-T07 / SL-SW.

findings.statement: D-6 has the process test check the triggers and the order of `npm ci` / `typecheck` / `test`. It does not check `permissions: contents: read` or `node-version: 22`. D-7 bases `security_impact: LOW` on `contents: read`, and the proposal names Node 22. A later edit that widens the permissions or changes Node passes the test silently.
findings.recommendation: Add to D-6: the workflow-level permissions are exactly `contents: read`, the job declares no wider permissions, and the Node version is 22.

findings.statement: The proposal (Impact) says 'Closes #28. Issue #27 is closed as not taken (grilling Q8)'. Grilling Q8 also has the maintainer check the protection of `main` and then close #20. No task in `tasks.md` closes #27 (label `wontfix` plus a comment, per rule `tracking`), and no task puts `Closes #28` in the PR body. Those acts are not verified.
findings.recommendation: Add a task: `Closes #28` in the impl-PR body; close #27 with `wontfix` and a comment citing Q8; verify both with `gh issue view`.

findings.statement: D-3 sets `concurrency: test-${{ github.ref }}` with `cancel-in-progress: true` for push to `main` too. Two quick merges cancel the run of the first merge commit, so that commit has no test result. A failure still shows on the later commit, but finding which commit broke `main` gets harder.
findings.recommendation: Use `cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}` so every commit on `main` keeps its run, or record that losing per-commit results on `main` is accepted.

assumptions.statement: `warrant sync` in D-1 p. 3 runs outside a Run and the guard admits it because `warrant` writes the generated files itself; not verified against the guard.
The D-5 table is the intended map (it matches grilling Q20); F-8 treats the ST-M01 wording as the defect, not the table.
Files under `.claude/agents/` are tracked in git, per the comment in `.gitignore`; not checked with `git ls-files`, because the review guard blocks it.
